text:
tess: Quick question — are we comfortable relying on HTTP/2 multiplexing for long-lived streaming from the edge to upstream, or should we gate it behind a config flag?
jamie: I worry about head-of-line blocking when lots of short requests share a long stream.
igor: If we do multiplexing we need clear limits: max concurrent streams per conn, per-tenant quotas, and a hard idle timeout.
chen: Also need to define retry semantics when a multiplexed connection dies midstream. Do we restart only idempotent requests or try to resume partially? :thinking_face:
sam: Resume is expensive. Unless the upstream supports tokenized checkpoints, fallback to restarting is simpler. We should avoid partial-resume unless the model request is explicitly checkpointable.
tess: Agreed. We already have prefix caching for KV, but resuming a streaming generation is not generically safe.
jamie: What about a lightweight resume token for cases where frontend wants to stitch partial outputs? Opt-in per route?
igor: Opt-in per route sounds ok, but we need an API: route config boolean + max-resume-window. Also define headers, e.g.:
```
Resume-Supported: true
Resume-Token: <opaque>
Resume-Window: 120000  # ms
```
chen: And who mints Resume-Token? Edge or upstream? If edge mints it we can guarantee opaque bounds; if upstream mints, we can avoid storing state. Tradeoffs.
sam: Edge-minted token lets us enforce quotas and TTLs. Upstream-minted is stateless for edge but couples to upstream semantics. I'd prefer edge token with HMAC so we don't keep DB state.
tess: Good call. Add HMAC + route salt, expire after X minutes. Document the token format so SDKs can understand resume semantics.
jamie: Back to retries: if a connection dies, we should retry at the request layer only for safe methods. For streaming, define three buckets: non-retryable (side-effectful), restartable (stateless generation), resumable (opt-in).
igor: We also should propagate a retry-attempt header so upstreams can detect duplicates: `X-Edge-Retry-Attempt: 0/1/2`.
chen: And we need idempotency keys for user-initiated side effects. But that's a separate UX ask.
ops-bot: deploy-bot deployed edge-proxy v2 to staging (build 2026.03.21-rc). :shipit:
tess: Can someone sketch the minimal config to add to route manifest? Something like: `multiplexing: auto|off|explicit`, `resume: enabled|disabled`, `resume-window-ms`, `max-streams-per-conn`.
sam: I'll draft a manifest snippet later today. Minimal example: 
```
route:
  multiplexing: auto
  max_streams_per_conn: 100
  streaming:
    resume: enabled
    resume_window_ms: 120000
    resume_hmac_salt: <env secret>
```
jamie: One more operational thing — telemetry. We must flag per-request whether it used multiplexing, whether it resumed, and retry counts. Needed for SLOs.
igor: Agree. Add metrics: edge.multiplexed.count, edge.resumed.count, edge.retry.attempts.histogram. Also record last-resume-failure-reason.
chen: Security: resume tokens should be single-use for a given stream id to avoid replay. HMAC + nonce or include expiry + stream-seq.
tess: Nice. Let's capture action items: @sam draft route manifest PR, @jamie add telemetry spec, @igor write token HMAC format + ttl, @chen evaluate upstream-minted vs edge-minted doc and post recommendation.
jamie: I'll also mock a failing scenario and run load tests with 200 concurrent short requests + 10 long streams to see head-of-line.
sam: Will do the PR today.
ops-bot: reminder: architecture sync tomorrow 11:00 — agenda: edge streaming behavior. :calendar:
tess: Thanks all — marking this resolved for now. We can reopen if load tests show issues. :eyes:
